days.title: Day 10 – Advanced CSS Grid
days.definition: Advanced CSS Grid builds upon basic grid knowledge with features like explicit and implicit grids, auto-placement algorithms, named grid lines, and complex responsive patterns.

explanation.main: Mastering advanced grid techniques enables sophisticated, responsive layouts with minimal code.
key_points: Implicit vs explicit grid tracks and how they're created
Understanding the auto-placement algorithm and how to control it with `grid-auto-flow`[citation:3]
Using named grid lines and areas for more maintainable layout code
Creating responsive grids without media queries using `auto-fit` and `minmax()`[citation:3]
Advanced item placement with line-based positioning and spanning

quiz.question: What does `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))` do?
options: Creates as many 200px columns as fit, then expands them equally
Creates responsive columns that collapse on mobile
quiz.answer: Creates as many 200px columns as fit, then expands them equally
quiz.reasoning: auto-fit creates as many columns as can fit with minimum 200px width, then distributes extra space equally (1fr) [citation:3].

quiz.question: What is the purpose of `grid-auto-flow: dense`?
options: Fills gaps in the grid by backfilling
quiz.answer: Fills gaps in the grid by backfilling
quiz.reasoning: The dense packing algorithm attempts to fill in holes earlier in the grid[citation:3].

quiz.question: How do you make a grid item span 2 columns and 3 rows?
quiz.reasoning: grid-column and grid-row properties control spanning across tracks[citation:8].

days.title: Day 11 – CSS Custom Properties (Variables)
days.definition: CSS Custom Properties (also called CSS Variables) allow you to store values in named variables that can be reused throughout your stylesheet, making CSS more maintainable and dynamic.

explanation.main: CSS Variables enable consistent theming and runtime style changes.
key_points: Variables are defined using `--variable-name: value;` syntax
Variables are accessed using the `var()` function
Variables can have fallback values: `var(--color, red)`
Variables are scoped to their selector and inherited by children
Variables can be modified with JavaScript for dynamic theming

quiz.question: Where are CSS variables typically defined for global use?
quiz.reasoning: :root selector targets the document root, making variables available globally.

quiz.question: What is the correct syntax to define a CSS variable?
quiz.reasoning: CSS variables are defined with double hyphen prefix: --variable-name: value;

quiz.question: How do you use a CSS variable with a fallback value?
quiz.reasoning: The var() function accepts a second parameter as fallback value.

days.title: Day 12 – CSS Transitions
days.definition: CSS Transitions allow you to smoothly animate property changes from one value to another over a specified duration, creating polished user interactions.

explanation.main: Transitions create smooth animations between state changes.
key_points: Four transition properties: property, duration, timing-function, and delay
Shorthand syntax: `transition: property duration timing-function delay`
Timing functions control acceleration: ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out
Multiple properties can be transitioned with different settings
Transitions trigger on pseudo-classes like :hover, :focus, :active

quiz.question: What is the correct order of transition shorthand properties?
quiz.reasoning: Shorthand order is: property duration timing-function delay[citation:4].

quiz.question: Which timing function starts slow, accelerates, then ends slow?
quiz.reasoning: ease starts slow, accelerates, then ends slow (default timing function)[citation:4].

quiz.question: How do you transition multiple properties with different durations?
options: Separate with commas: transition: color 0.3s, transform 0.5s
quiz.answer: Separate with commas: transition: color 0.3s, transform 0.5s
quiz.reasoning: Multiple transitions are separated by commas.

days.title: Day 13 – CSS Animations & @keyframes
days.definition: CSS Animations using @keyframes allow complex, multi-step animations with full control over intermediate states, timing, and repetition.

explanation.main: @keyframes define the animation sequence while animation properties control its execution.
key_points: @keyframes rule defines the animation sequence from 0% to 100%
Animation properties: name, duration, timing-function, delay, iteration-count, direction, fill-mode, play-state[citation:4]
Keyframes can use 'from'/'to' keywords or percentage values
Animations can run infinite times or specific counts
Fill-mode controls styles before/after animation (forwards, backwards, both)

options: Reverses animation on every other iteration
quiz.answer: Reverses animation on every other iteration

quiz.question: What does animation-fill-mode: forwards do?

days.title: Day 14 – CSS Transforms
days.definition: CSS Transforms allow you to modify the coordinate space of elements, enabling translation, rotation, scaling, and skewing in 2D and 3D space.

explanation.main: Transforms change an element's appearance without affecting document flow.
key_points: 2D transforms: translate(), rotate(), scale(), skew(), matrix()
3D transforms add Z-axis: translate3d(), rotate3d(), scale3d()
Transform-origin sets the point around which transformations occur
Multiple transforms can be combined in one transform property
Transforms can be animated with transitions and animations

days.title: Day 15 – Advanced Selectors & Specificity
days.definition: Advanced CSS selectors and specificity rules allow precise targeting of elements and understanding of which styles take precedence when multiple rules apply.

explanation.main: Mastering selectors and specificity is crucial for writing maintainable, scalable CSS.
key_points: Attribute selectors: [attribute], [attribute=value], [attribute~=value], [attribute|=value], [attribute^=value], [attribute$=value], [attribute*=value]
Combinators: descendant (space), child (>), adjacent sibling (+), general sibling (~)
Specificity hierarchy: inline styles > IDs > classes/attributes/pseudo-classes > elements/pseudo-elements
!important declaration overrides all specificity (use sparingly)
Cascade order: importance, source order, specificity
